messages: Board lead: my 1250 mm² claim (2800 mm³) carries about 50 mm² of slack above the routability floor. I'm giving that back and moving to 1205 mm² (2699 mm³), which frees about 101 mm³. The floor is about 1197 mm² (2681 mm³). I'm holding a few mm² of margin because routability falls off quickly below 0.95, and I can't go lower without risking the 10-layer routing on the W1000. The interior is still over by about 1145 mm³, so I OBJECT until the whole ledger balances. Battery, structure, acoustics and antenna will need to find most of the rest.

Battery lead: I'm at 3786 mm³ and 59.78 h, so I'm already marginally short of the ~60 h target. The 4.73 mm cell plus the 2.24 mm board gives a 6.97 mm stack against the 7.1 mm limit. I can't give back much without breaking runtime, and the siren's 3 h endurance also draws on this same energy. I'm probing smaller cells to find the runtime cost per mm³. Caseback is at 1120 of 1143 mm², so there's little room to widen the footprint. I'd rather see the interior overage closed by antenna, structure and acoustics trimming to their actual minimums. I OBJECT, since the ledger is still over by about 1145 mm³.

Antenna lead: I'm holding 1500 mm³ this round because I don't yet know how L5 efficiency (0.208 now) falls as V_ant shrinks. I'm probing 1200 and 1000 mm³ to get that slope, plus a 1.1 mm wall. Each 0.1 mm of wall returns 150 mm³ to every domain, and thinner titanium should detune the antenna less. Structure lead, please say whether 1.1 mm is feasible. I'll offer a concrete give-back next round once I have the numbers. I'm not giving up the L5 margin blindly. I OBJECT because the ledger is still over by 1145 mm³.

Thermal: I'm at 320 mm² (250 mm³) and skin temperature is exactly 43.0 C, so I have no margin and can't give volume back at 1.2 mm wall. The spreader is also only about 22% of the 1143 mm² caseback pool, so it isn't the main pressure there. I'm probing how a thinner wall (1.1 mm) changes skin temperature, and what spreader area would restore margin if it runs hotter. Structure lead, the 1.1 mm answer matters to me too. I OBJECT because the interior is still over by 1145 mm³.

Structure: pressure margin is 1.438 at 1.2 mm wall, 1800 mm³ ribs and a 9 mm² port, so I fail the 1.5 requirement. A 1.1 mm wall is not feasible, because it would lower the margin further. I won't give back volume yet.

I'm probing three ways to close the gap:
- More rib volume.
- A smaller port. Acoustics, please tell me the minimum port that still gives 86 dB and good intelligibility, because a port cut costs nobody interior volume.
- A thicker wall. This costs 150 mm³ per 0.1 mm, so I expect it to be the most expensive option.

Next round I'll claim the cheapest combination. I OBJECT.

Acoustics: my siren fails. It needs 9.08 W at the driver against a 1.0 W limit. Endurance is 0.34 h on the current battery, against a 3 h target. The resonance sits at 5.6 kHz, which looks mistuned for a siren. I can't answer the structure lead's minimum port yet. A smaller port will probably worsen the siren, so I'm not offering one. I'm dropping the mesh to its 20 rayl floor and lengthening the outlet to pull the resonance down. I'm probing the port, the outlet length and a smaller volume to find where 1 W works. I'll commit to any volume give-back once I see those results. OBJECT.

Haptics: force is 1.069 N at 350 mm³, and the requirement is 0.9 N. Force scales roughly linearly, about 0.00305 N per mm³, so the floor is about 295 mm³. I'm giving back 45 mm³ and moving to 305 mm³, which should give about 0.93 N. That leaves a few percent of margin without going to the edge. I can't go lower without failing my own requirement.

The ledger is still over by about 1100 mm³, so I OBJECT. My give-back is small, so the real closure has to come from the large pools: structure, acoustics, antenna and battery. Acoustics, please check whether the siren fix can come from tuning rather than extra volume.

NFC: read range is 18.2 mm against a 10 mm requirement, so I have real slack and will give it back. I'm cutting from 500 to 390 mm³ (loop 250, ferrite 140), which frees 110 mm³. I don't yet know how steeply range falls with volume, so I'm probing down to the bounds (180/110) to find the floor. Next round I'll claim close to whatever still gives ≥10 mm with a few mm of margin. The loop volume sits in the perimeter keepout, so cutting it also eases that pool. The interior is still over, so I OBJECT. Antenna, structure and acoustics hold the big numbers.

Board: I'm trimming from 1205 to 1199 mm² (2686 mm³), which frees about 13 mm³. Probes put routability at 0.95 at 1197 mm² and 0.956 at 1205 mm², so 1199 mm² should give about 0.952. I'm keeping 2 mm² above the floor because the evaluator rounds. That is my last real give-back, since the floor is 1197 mm² (2681 mm³).

The ledger is still about 990 mm³ over, and the board is only 2.7k of the 12.2k claimed. The closure has to come from structure (1800 mm³), acoustics (1460 mm³), antenna (1500 mm³) and battery. I'm probing 1197, 1198 and 1200 mm² to confirm the floor. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Battery: I can't give volume back. Runtime is 59.78 h at 3786 mm³, already under the ~60 h target. My probes put the slope at about 0.0158 h per mm³: 3700 mm³ gives 58.42 h and 3900 mm³ gives 61.58 h. 60 h needs about 3800 mm³, so I'm claiming 3800 (+14 mm³), the minimum for the target. Every mm³ I cut costs about 0.016 h, and the siren's 3 h endurance draws on the same energy.

The stack is fine at 4.73 mm against the 7.1 mm limit, and the caseback is 1120 of 1143 mm². I'm not asking for more footprint.

The overage is 976 mm³. It has to close in structure, acoustics and antenna. Acoustics, a siren needing 9 W is a tuning problem, and a bigger cell won't fix it. I OBJECT.

Antenna: the L5 efficiency slope is steep and roughly linear: 0.093 at 1000 mm³, 0.133 at 1200 and 0.208 at 1500. That is about 0.00025 per mm³ above 1200, so every 100 mm³ I give up costs about 12% of my L5 efficiency. A 1.1 mm wall only adds +0.009, so it isn't worth the structure risk, and I agree with the structure lead on 1.2 mm.

I'm giving back 50 mm³ now, moving to 1450. I'm probing 1400 and 1300 to find where L5 becomes unacceptable. I'm also probing 1.3 mm wall at 1500, since structure may need a thicker wall and I want its detuning cost. The perimeter keepout is fine at 1750 of 2400 mm³ claimed. The interior is still about 990 mm³ over, so I OBJECT.

Thermal: skin temperature is 43.0 C at 320 mm² and 1.2 mm wall, so I have no margin. My probes show a slope of about 0.0105 C per mm² (340 mm² gives 42.79 C). A 1.1 mm wall changes almost nothing (-0.01 C). Structure, that means a thicker wall costs me only about +0.01 C. I'm adding 5 mm² (+4 mm³) so rounding or a 1.3 mm wall doesn't push me over 43 C. That is my only real margin, and I can't give volume back.

The caseback is fine at about 1125 of 1143 mm². The roughly 990 mm³ overage has to close in structure, acoustics and antenna. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Structure: my probes give these margins.
- Wall +0.1 mm adds about 0.197, at a cost of 150 mm³ to everyone.
- Port 9→7 mm² adds about 0.124 and costs no volume.
- Ribs +300 mm³ add only about 0.025.

Ribs are the weakest margin per mm³, so I'm cutting them to the 1400 floor. That frees 400 mm³ and costs about 0.033 margin. I'll recover that with a wall of about 1.25 mm, which costs 75 mm³ and adds about 0.1. Net, the interior gains about 325 mm³ and the margin lands near 1.50, so it's thin.

Acoustics, I'm not asking you for a smaller port yet. If 8 mm² fixes the siren tuning, I'd take it, since it gives me 0.06 of margin for free.

I'm prob

Acoustics: my siren still fails, at 7.67 W against the 1.0 W limit. The last probes show the trend. Port 9→7 mm² cut power from 7.67 to 6.3 W and moved resonance from 5275 to 4803 Hz. Longer outlet and lower mesh resistance also help. A smaller volume barely changes power, but SII drops, from 88.4 to 85.3 at 1200 mm³. So the fix is tuning, not volume.

Structure, I'm taking 7 mm² now, which gives you about 0.12 of margin for free. I'm probing 3-5 mm² with a 3.5 mm outlet to find where the resonance lands. I'll hold 1460 mm³ until I know where 1 W is reached. After that I'll give back volume with the SII cost known.

Haptics: I'm trimming from 305 to 300 mm³, which frees 5 mm³. My probes gave 0.901 N at 295 and 0.916 N at 300, so 300 keeps about 1.8% margin over 0.9 N. I'm not going to 295, because 0.901 N is inside evaluator rounding. This is my real floor, since force is linear in volume.

The interior is still about 940 mm³ over, and haptics is only 300 of the 12.1k claimed. The closure has to come from the large pools.
- **Structure:** ribs from 1800 toward 1400 would free about 400 mm³.
- **Acoustics:** 1460 mm³ is held until the siren tuning lands, and that is the biggest open item.
- **Antenna:** 1450 mm³ is still being traded against L5 efficiency.

I OBJECT until the interior balances.

NFC: my probes show range stays well above 10 mm all the way down to the bounds. At 180/110 it is 12.7 mm, which is 27% margin. I can't cut further, because those are the minimum bounds. I'm claiming loop 180 and ferrite 110, which frees 100 mm³ from interior and 70 mm³ from the perimeter keepout.

The ledger still has about 840 mm³ to close. That has to come from structure ribs (about 400 mm³ on offer), antenna and acoustics. If the ledger gets tight, I can tell you what 12.7 mm at the floor is worth. I'm probing 180/130 and 200/110 to price the next mm³ if anyone needs me to take volume back. OBJECT until the interior balances.

Board: I'm moving from 1199 to 1198 mm² (2683 mm³). Routability is 0.951 there, and 0.95 at 1197 is the hard floor, so I'm keeping 1 mm² above it for evaluator rounding. This is a real give-back, but only about 2 mm³, so it doesn't close the gap.

The interior is still 839 mm³ over, and the board is already near its minimum. The closure has to come from the large pools:
- **Structure:** ribs from 1800 to 1400 would free about 400 mm³.
- **Acoustics:** 1460 mm³ should drop once the siren tuning lands and the SII cost is known.
- **Antenna:** 1450 mm³ is still being traded against L5 efficiency.

I'm probing 1196 and 1197.5 mm² to check how sharp the routability cliff is below the floor. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Battery: I'm holding at 3800 mm³ and 800 mm². That gives 60.0 h, exactly on target, and the stack is 4.75 + 2.24 = 6.99 mm against the 7.1 mm limit. Runtime depends only on volume (about 0.0158 h/mm³), so changing footprint frees nothing from the interior pool. Each 10 mm³ I give up costs about 0.16 h, and the siren's 3 h endurance draws on the same energy.

The overage is 837 mm³. The closure has to come from structure ribs (about 400 mm³ on offer), acoustics (1460 mm³) and antenna. Acoustics, the siren is a port and tuning problem, so please don't ask for battery volume. I'm probing 3790 and 3780 to price a small give-back if the ledger ends up within about 20 mm³ of balance. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Antenna: I'm giving back another 50 mm³, from 1450 to 1400. L5 efficiency drops from 0.194 to 0.181, about 7% relative, and the probe confirms the roughly linear slope of 0.00025 per mm³. At 1300 it is 0.156 (-20%), so I won't go below 1400 without a stated L5 threshold. Nobody has given me one.

Structure, a wall of 1.25 mm costs me about 0.0045 at 1500 mm³ (a 1.3 mm wall costs 0.009), which I can accept. Your ribs cut to 1400 is the right first move.

Acoustics, 1460 mm³ is the largest remaining claim. Please say what you can give back once the port tuning is known.

The interior is still over by about 790 mm³ after my cut, so I OBJECT. I'm probing 1350 and 1250 mm³ to see whether the slope holds.

Thermal: I'm holding 325 mm² (254 mm³). Skin temperature is 42.94 C against the 43.0 C limit. Probes put 310 mm² at 43.12 C (fail) and 330 mm² at 42.89 C. The slope is about 0.0105 C per mm², so every 1 mm² I cut costs about 0.01 C. A 1.3 mm wall adds only 0.02 C at 325 mm², so structure's 1.25 mm wall is safe for me (about 42.95 C). I can't go below about 322 mm² without losing the rounding margin, and that frees only 2 mm³.

The interior is still 787 mm³ over, and thermal is only 254 mm³ of it. The closure has to come from structure (ribs 1800 to 1400), acoustics (1460 mm³) and antenna. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Structure: I'm cutting ribs from 1800 to the 1400 floor, which frees 400 mm³. I'm keeping the wall at 1.2 mm.

By my estimate the margin at 1400 ribs, 1.2 mm wall and 7 mm² port is about 1.53 against the 1.5 limit. That is thin, but it passes, and it needs no wall increase. A thicker wall would cost everyone 75 mm³ or more, so I'm dropping the 1.25 mm idea.

The ledger is still about 387 mm³ over. Acoustics (1460 mm³) now has to give most of that back. Battery, antenna and board have already given what they can.

If acoustics lands on a port of 4-5 mm², I can trade it for a 1.1 mm wall, which frees another 150 mm³ for everyone. I'm probing that now. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Acoustics: I'm giving back 260 mm³, from 1460 to 1200. The 1200 probe at port 4 and split 0.7 gave the lowest siren power so far, 4.0 W, so smaller volume doesn't hurt the siren. The cost is SII, which falls to 85.1 from 88.4. Nobody has stated an SII floor, so please tell me if 85 is a problem.

I'm taking the port to 4 mm², which gives structure about 0.19 of margin and may justify its 1.1 mm wall. That would return 150 mm³ to everyone. The siren still fails at 4 W against the 1.0 W limit, so I OBJECT. I'm probing split, which I haven't varied yet, and a smaller volume.

Haptics: force is linear at about 0.0032 N per mm³, so 298 mm³ gives 0.910 N, 1.1% over the 0.9 N limit. I'm going from 300 to 298 and giving back 2 mm³. I won't go lower because 296 mm³ gives 0.904 N, which is inside evaluator rounding.

After acoustics' 260 mm³ give-back and the board's 1 mm², the interior is about 125 mm³ over. Haptics can't close that.

The closure has to come from a structure wall of 1.1 mm (150 mm³ freed) and from acoustics' siren tuning. Nothing in my domain depends on port, wall or battery. A 1.1 mm wall costs haptics nothing. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

NFC: I'm at both minimum bounds, loop 180 and ferrite 110 mm³, so I have nothing left to give. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, which is 27% margin. Going to the bounds saved 100 mm³ of interior and 70 mm³ of keepout. Taking back volume would only raise range (200/110 gives 13.4 mm), and nobody needs that.

After acoustics' 260 mm³ cut, I estimate the interior is still about 125 mm³ over. Structure's 1.1 mm wall (150 mm³ freed) would close it. I can't probe the wall, but NFC range shouldn't depend on it, and I can live with that.

I OBJECT only because the interior doesn't balance and the siren still fails. My own requirement is met.

Board: I'm holding at 1198 mm² (2683 mm³), routability 0.951. My probes show 1197.5 gives 0.950 and passes, 1196 gives 0.949 and fails, and 1190 gives 0.944. The cliff is shallow, about 0.0008 per mm². Dropping to 1197.5 would free only about 1 mm³, and I want the 0.5 mm² margin against evaluator rounding. I can't close the gap. Routability doesn't depend on wall, port or battery, so structure's 1.1 mm wall (150 mm³ freed) costs me nothing.

The ledger shows the interior 385 mm³ over, with acoustics still at 1460. Acoustics' proposed cut to 1200 would leave it about 125 mm³ over, and a 1.1 mm wall would close that. The siren also still fails. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Battery: I'm holding at 3800 mm³ and 800 mm², which gives 60.0 h with the stack at 6.99 mm. A give-back costs about 0.16 h per 10 mm³, and the siren's 3 h endurance draws on the same energy.

The numbers close without more battery volume. The ledger still shows acoustics at 1460. If acoustics lands at 1200 and structure moves to a 1.1 mm wall, the claims fall to about 11,324 mm³ against a pool of about 11,350 mm³. That leaves roughly 26 mm³ spare. If the final gap is under about 20 mm³ I can give 10 to 20 mm³, which costs 0.16 to 0.32 h. I won't cut for a larger gap.

Structure, please confirm that the 1.1 mm wall passes at 4 mm². Acoustics, the 4 W siren is your open item, not a battery-volume question. I OBJECT until the interior balances.

Antenna: I'm holding at 1400 mm³ (L5 0.181). The slope is a steady 0.00024 per mm³, so the cuts so far are costing real L5.

The closure path is clear. Acoustics at 1200 leaves the interior about 125 mm³ over, and structure's 1.1 mm wall frees 150 mm³. A thinner wall also helps me: 1.25 mm cost 0.004, so 1.1 mm should return about +0.004 of L5. If the gap is then under about 25 mm³, I can give 15-20 mm³ and still sit near 0.18. I'm probing that now.

Without a 1.1 mm wall I won't go below 1400. Acoustics, please hold the 1200 mm³ claim and fix the siren with the port and split. Structure, please confirm the wall. I OBJECT because the interior is still over.

Thermal: I'm holding at 325 mm² (254 mm³), skin temperature 42.94 C against the 43.0 C limit. I can live with structure's 1.1 mm wall. Thickening the wall raises my temperature (1.25 mm added about 0.01 C), so thinning it should lower it slightly. I'm probing 1.1 mm at 325, 320 and 318 mm² to confirm. If it holds, I can cut 5-7 mm² and return about 4-5 mm³. That is small, so the closure still depends on acoustics at 1200 mm³ and the 1.1 mm wall. Structure, please confirm the wall passes at a 4 mm² port. I OBJECT because the interior is still over.

Structure: the 1.1 mm wall passes only with a small port. My probes at 1.1 mm and 1400 mm³ ribs gave margin 1.527 (pass) at a 4 mm² port and 1.465 (fail) at 5 mm². The ledger still shows the port at 7 mm², where 1.1 mm fails. I'm moving to 1.1 mm now, which frees 150 mm³ for everyone, on one condition: acoustics must lock the port at ≤4.0 mm². Acoustics, please confirm 4.0 or lower, because 4.5 is untested. I'm probing 4.5 mm² and a 1.0 mm wall at 3 mm². I OBJECT until the port shows 4 in the ledger and the interior balances.

Acoustics: I'm locking the port at 4.0 mm² for structure's 1.1 mm wall, and moving to 1200 mm³. With wall 1.1, that puts the claims at about 11,325 mm³ against the 11,350 mm³ pool, roughly 25 mm³ spare. Battery and antenna can take that as they see fit.

My open item is the siren, which still fails. At 1200 mm³, port 4 and split 0.7 it needs 4.0 W against the 1.0 W limit. I'm not asking for battery volume, because the siren is a tuning problem. I haven't yet varied h_out, which is currently at its 3.5 maximum, or split away from 0.7. SII is about 85, and I still need someone to state a floor. I OBJECT until the siren passes.

Haptics: my requirement is met. At 298 mm³ force is 0.910 N against the 0.9 N limit. My probes show 295 mm³ gives 0.901 N and 296 gives 0.904 N, so I'm moving to 296 mm³ (0.904 N) and returning 2 mm³. I'm keeping about 0.4% margin for evaluator rounding and won't go lower.

Haptics doesn't depend on wall, port or battery, so structure's 1.1 mm wall at a 4 mm² port costs me nothing. The interior now balances with about 25 mm³ spare, which battery and antenna can split.

I'm objecting only because the ledger still has the siren failing at 4 W against the 1.0 W limit. That is a program goal, not a volume problem. Acoustics, please vary h_out and split next.

NFC: I'm holding at the bounds, loop 180 mm³ and ferrite 110 mm³. Read range is 12.7 mm against the 10 mm requirement, and I have nothing left to give back. Neither wall nor port affects NFC, so the 1.1 mm wall at a 4 mm² port costs me nothing.

Board: my requirement is met. At 1198 mm², routability is 0.951. Last round's probes at 1197.5 and 1197.0 both passed at 0.950, and 1196 failed. I'm moving to 1197.5 mm² (about 2682 mm³), which returns about 1 mm³. That is small, but it keeps 0.5 mm² above the lowest tested pass. I won't go lower, because the cliff is steep below 1197.

Wall, port and battery don't affect routability, so the 1.1 mm wall at a 4 mm² port costs me nothing. The interior balances with about 28 mm³ spare. Acoustics should have that spare first if the siren needs it. I OBJECT only because the siren still fails.

The siren is acoustics' open item. Siren endurance draws on my cell energy, but 4 W against a 1.0 W limit is a 4x gap, and no battery volume closes that. Acoustics, please vary h_out and split.

If you find the 3 h endurance needs a little energy, tell me. I can take up to the 28 mm³ spare, and I'm probing 3820 and 3828 mm³ to see how much runtime that adds. The caseback plane has 18 mm² spare if footprint matters.

I OBJECT only because the siren still fails.

Structure: my requirement is met at a 1.1 mm wall, 1400 mm³ of ribs and a 4.0 mm² port, with a pressure margin of 1.527.

Acoustics, if the siren needs a bigger port, here is what I can give you:
